sources.title: Medium combustion plant (MCP): comply with emission limit values
sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra / NRW / Welsh Government
facts: MCP ELVs depend on plant type, fuel and technology, and monitoring is required to demonstrate permit compliance.
New MCP monitoring starts within 4 months of permit issue or operation start, whichever is later.
An ELV or compliance requirement is a regulatory standard and is not itself an observed annual GHG mass or parcel measurement.
sources.guard: Keep ELV, monitoring requirement and operating-hour evidence separate from measured pollutant mass and parcel attribution.

sources.title: Medium combustion plant: apply for an environmental permit
sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra / NRW / Welsh Government
facts: MCPD standalone permits cover SO2, NOx and dust emissions to air and may be standard rules, simple bespoke or complex bespoke.
Applications can require plant location, thermal input, fuel, operating hours, abatement and monitoring information.
Application or screening inputs are regulatory evidence; they are not automatically verified site measurements or cadastral parcel GHG.
sources.guard: Do not promote permit-application inputs, screening outcomes or stated plant characteristics to verified measured parcel emissions.

sources.title: Medium combustion plant: when you need a permit
sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra / NRW / Welsh Government
facts: MCPD controls apply to in-scope combustion units from 1 MWth to below 50 MWth.
Permit and compliance dates vary by whether plant is new or existing and by thermal capacity.
Capacity, permit scope and compliance dates identify regulatory applicability, not actual emission quantities.
sources.guard: Treat capacity and permit-scope facts as applicability evidence only, not as measured emissions.

sources.title: Medium combustion plant: screening tool
facts: SCAIL Combustion models NOx and SO2 effects on sensitive habitat sites from source and stack parameters.
Guidance derives screening emission rates from ELVs and normalised volumetric flow at common reference conditions.
Screening outputs and derived rates are model inputs or predictions and must not be treated as observed parcel GHG.
sources.guard: Separate modelled screening rates and habitat impact predictions from observed stack results and parcel-level GHG.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions: low risk MCPs and specified generators
facts: Guidance provides a standardised approach to stack-gas monitoring for low-risk MCPs and specified generators.
The 2026 update extends scope to simple bespoke permits and adds use of MCERTS-certified low-risk monitors for continuous monitoring.
A monitoring standard or certified instrument is quality evidence, not the monitored concentration, flow or annual mass itself.
sources.guard: Do not substitute monitoring-method compliance or MCERTS certification for actual measurement results.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions: techniques and standards for periodic monitoring
facts: The index selects periodic monitoring techniques and standards for stack emissions to air.
The 2026 guidance includes recognised techniques and standards for CO2 and many other substances.
Selecting a method establishes measurement quality requirements; it does not create a measurement result.
sources.guard: Method selection and reference standards must stay separate from concentration, flow, duration and mass observations.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions: standards for continuous monitoring and sampling
facts: Guidance specifies standards for CEMS, DAHS, long-term samplers and predictive emissions monitoring systems.
Continuous monitoring quality assurance governs instruments and data handling.
System certification and calibration requirements are not emissions observations by themselves.
sources.guard: Keep CEMS/DAHS/PEMS standards and calibration evidence distinct from validated emissions data and parcel binding.

sources.title: Monitoring emissions to air, land and water (MCERTS)
facts: MCERTS covers monitoring performance standards for permit holders across air, water, land and environmental data systems.
Certification supports measurement quality and competence.
Certification status alone does not prove a specific emission value or its time, unit, facility or parcel scope.
sources.guard: Use MCERTS as provenance/quality metadata only; require the actual validated result for emissions claims.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions: carbon capture plants with solvent-based abatement
facts: Guidance standardises monitoring of stack emissions from post-combustion carbon capture plants using solvent-based abatement.
It is monitoring guidance for regulated carbon-capture plant, not a dataset of captured or emitted CO2.
Capture-system presence or monitoring scope cannot be converted to capture rate, stored CO2 or emitted CO2 without measured evidence.
sources.guard: Preserve carbon-capture chain boundaries and require explicit measured quantities before any captured/stored/emitted mass claim.

sources.title: Decarbonisation readiness in environmental permit applications
facts: Guidance explains decarbonisation readiness for relevant electricity-generating combustion plants in England.
It applies to environmental permit applications submitted on or after 28 February 2026.
Readiness for carbon capture or hydrogen conversion is design/permitting evidence, not evidence that capture or conversion is operating.
sources.guard: Do not translate decarbonisation or carbon-capture readiness into actual capture performance or avoided emissions.

sources.title: Landfill operators: environmental permits - Manage landfill gas
facts: Operators must collect landfill gas and control migration and atmospheric release for relevant landfills.
Gas extraction, utilisation, flaring and related monitoring data must be reviewed and inconsistencies investigated.
A gas management plan or control-system description is not itself a measured methane or GHG release.
sources.guard: Require explicit landfill-gas monitoring results, units, period and site geometry before emissions or parcel claims.

sources.title: Landfill operators: environmental permits - Monitor and report your performance
facts: Landfill permits require monitoring and reporting of site performance including landfill gas, point sources and other environmental media where relevant.
Monitoring plans must address uncertainty, QA/QC, methods, points, reporting and interpretation.
A monitoring obligation or plan does not establish the value of an emission until an actual validated result is available.
sources.guard: Keep monitoring-plan requirements separate from observed values; require result, uncertainty, unit, period and spatial scope.
